Do Not Hardcode the Clincoo API Host in Editor Files

A host written in JS breaks preview when the domain changes. Read a public env value, not a fixed string.

This article is available in: Indonesia · English

Many Clincoo projects paste https://app.clincoo.buzz straight into fetch. After a staging move, every file must change by hand.

Store the host in a public env variable, then read it once in a config module on editor.clincoo.buzz. Other files only import that object.

Test in preview: change the env value, reload, confirm requests hit the new host. If they still hit the old one, a literal remains.

Ask AI to find https literals in the project. Do not ask it to rewrite the whole app.

Clincoo on app.clincoo.buzz stays the same; only the host source changes.
